figures.caption: No introduced change. Points show observed proportions; bars show 95% Wilson intervals. Dashed line: 5% target. Per-batch PSI and fixed PSI 0.1 are ablations without horizon control. Outcome and combined monitors include labels.
figures.name: 01_stream_false_alarms
figures.title: Does a 20-batch monitoring run raise a false alarm?

figures.caption: Forty independent streams per cell; color is the probability of any alert during 15 post-change batches. A=1,B=1 alone shifts. Zero can reflect inadequate subgroup counts, weak effects, or the error-control cost. Cell intervals are in the source CSV.
figures.name: 02_detection_map
figures.title: Where does input-drift monitoring work?

figures.caption: Paired complete streams; both methods use the same groups and a 5% horizon budget. Percentile bootstrap intervals use 5,000 paired resamples. Positive favors PSI; negative favors KS. Degenerate intervals at identical paired outcomes do not prove population equality.
figures.name: 03_psi_vs_ks
figures.title: Does PSI add value beyond subgrouping?

figures.caption: Batch n=250, shift=1.4 SD; 40 streams per share. Ordinary tests require 50 records per batch; accumulation requires 100 per block. Undetected targets are assigned the 15-batch horizon, not dropped. Delay intervals describe a restricted mean; coverage uses Wilson intervals.
figures.name: 04_coverage_delay
figures.title: More small-group coverage can come with a delay

figures.caption: Forty streams per condition; 95% Wilson intervals. Only the full swap preserves aggregate and single-attribute input distributions exactly. Aggregate alerts there are false alarms. Points are offset horizontally to expose overlap; lines only guide the eye.
figures.name: 05_cancellation
figures.title: How much does the cancellation example matter?

figures.caption: 250 no-change streams; 40 per other scenario. Outcome audits test TPR decrease, FPR increase and accuracy decrease even when input checks are quiet; labels arrive immediately. The combined monitor splits its 5% budget between channels. 95% Wilson intervals; no universal fairness verdict.
figures.name: 06_input_and_outcome
figures.title: Input change and prediction deterioration are different signals

figures.caption: Average the 15 post-change batches within each stream, then estimate paired mean changes over 40 independent streams; bars are 95% t intervals, not simultaneous intervals. TPR: actual positives correctly predicted; FPR: actual negatives incorrectly predicted positive. Small denominators remain in the source table.
figures.name: 07_group_outcomes
figures.title: Check what happened to predictions inside each group

figures.caption: UCI Adult (Becker & Kohavi, CC BY 4.0): 20 repeats per condition within each of three fixed role splits. Markers distinguish splits; 95% Wilson intervals are conditional resampling uncertainty. This is an injected sampling shift, not observed chronological drift or new independent populations.
figures.name: 08_public_data
figures.title: Does the result persist across public-data splits?

figures.caption: Each point is one fixed method, not a threshold-swept ROC curve. Detection averages the 12 equally weighted group-share/shift cells at the stated batch size (480 streams); false alarms use 250 null streams. Real-world case frequencies may differ. Point overlap is possible; all values are in the CSV.
figures.name: 09_operating_tradeoff
figures.title: A high alert rate is useful only with a low false-alarm cost

figures.caption: First saved repeat (0) from each named scenario, selected by index rather than outcome. Shading begins at the batch-6 intervention. Filled markers: corrected alerts; hollow: no alert. These are two illustrative trajectories, not detection-rate estimates. Panel y-scales differ; all observations are generated.
figures.name: 10_drift_over_time
figures.title: Watch a hidden shift appear over time

summary: Revision 2: 1,820 synthetic streams and 120 conditional Adult streams; 20 batches per stream. Accumulation improved detection in the fixed grid; PSI did not outperform KS overall. Input drift alone did not establish prediction harm or fairness. Methods, uncertainty and failures remain visible.
